column7: The body of build_mcp_headers: picks MCP-Session-Id from the caller's identity bucket only, and for a lent credential (CredentialOrigin::Lent) reads no gateway OAuth token and adds no operator static header, so a per-user listener never sends the gateway's credential (MIK-8833 C6).
Builds a lent request's headers through build_headers with CredentialOrigin::Lent; passing Gateway here would add the gateway's credential to a subscriber's request.
Split from post_and_read: binds a session id the upstream mints to the caller's own MCP-Session-Id bucket only, for a call's answer and for a per-user listener's send alike.
The body of open_listen: builds the listen POST with who's headers and sends it through who, healing the gateway's session only for OpenAs::Gateway; refuses with 404 when that session cannot heal.
The body of open_session_stream: bounds the untrusted upstream stream with SseDecoder FRAME_CAP and drops any note not admitted by watched.admits before it crosses the channel; sends as who.
Chooses the gateway's headers or a lent request's (no gateway credential); a wrong arm would send the gateway's credential as a subscriber (MIK-8833 invariant 2).
Sends a lent request only inside its CredentialSource's with_credential, which merges the subscriber's credential and may refuse; a refusal sends nothing.
On a lent session's 404, drops the carried session id from that subscriber's own bucket only, never the gateway's or another subscriber's.
Builds a Streamable HTTP listener session only with a credential source and a bucket of its own; None otherwise, so nothing is sent without the subscriber's credential.
Always OpenAs::Lent with this session's bucket and source; a Gateway arm here would send the gateway's credential.
Sends one request through who and reads its answer into this subscriber's bucket only (read_answer with Some(bucket)).
Runs the subscriber's own initialize in their own bucket when the peer keeps sessions; never reuses the gateway's session.
Forwards a per-user listener's mint to MetaMcp::mint_listener_credential, the audited path; refuses when the gateway is stopping.

Answers events/lease itself, never forwarding it; the owner is the events owner principal subscribe keys rows by, and the token is only the caller's own passthrough header, moved into a wiping buffer. EventsHub::lease decides.
Derives the key that separates per-user listeners (stable actor id and audience, or the exchange cache key); two subscribers with one key would share a listener and each other's events.
Derives a managed account's observation key from its digest and audience, length-prefixed so two accounts never share a listener; refuses an undigestible account.
